stem: A routine equipment check is allowed, but the next troubleshooting step requires opening a guarded panel. What should Technician I do?
choices: Open the guarded panel if the alarm is urgent and only a visual inspection is needed.
Stop at the authorized operator-care boundary and refer the protected troubleshooting step to qualified personnel.
Ask a more experienced technician to open the panel while the learner observes.
Acknowledge or disable the alarm temporarily so the equipment can remain in service until maintenance arrives.
rationale: Routine operator checks do not authorize access behind guards or into areas that may expose workers to hazardous energy. Technician I should stop at the defined boundary and escalate to qualified personnel. Urgency, experience, or observation by another worker does not replace the required servicing and energy-control authorization.
